review.why: Clarifies brand messaging with the seven-part StoryBrand framework and scores copy against it out of ten.
review.summary: Walks through seven elements: a character with one desire, a problem at three levels, a guide with empathy and authority, a plan, a call to action, stakes and success. Each has principle, rationale, applications and copy patterns. It adds a one-liner formula with a repeat-after-one-hearing test, a seven-row diagnostic score and a table of common mistakes.
strengths: Scores any copy and states the changes needed to reach the top score
Concrete copy patterns and examples for every element
Ethical rule: a button must not call a paid action free
cautions: Presents one framework as the whole method
Six reference files (brand script, sequences, wireframe, one-liners) are not read here
Ends with an affiliate-tagged book link and an author bio
